translation: The Blessed Lord said: The ancient sages describe the manifest universe as an immortal banyan tree (Ashvattha) whose roots extend upward into the Supreme Divine and whose branches stretch downward into matter. Its leaves represent the literal ritualistic hymns; he who understands this tree possesses genuine knowledge of the Veda (veda-vit).
simple_explanation: This classic metaphor is rooted directly in Rigveda (1.24.7) and Katha Upanishad. The tree is inverted because its generating power comes from above—from the transcendent Divine Consciousness—while its physical leaves and fruits grow down here on earth. It is called Ashvattha (literally, "that which will not remain identical tomorrow") to indicate the volatile, changing nature of the material universe.

translation: Nourished and thickened by the three modes of nature, with sensory objects acting as its fresh sprouts, its branches stretch downward into human life and upward into celestial realms. Its secondary roots extend downward into the human world, locking the soul into the binding loops of reward-driven action (karmanubandhini).

Its real structural layout cannot be grasped by a superficial observation down here on earth— neither its final end, nor its primeval origin, nor its continuous foundation can be mapped. Therefore, sharpening the heavy, solid axe of non-attachment (asanga-shastrena), one must fearlessly hack down this deep-rooted tree.

Thereafter, one must seek out that absolute Goal upon reaching which a traveler never slips back into the friction of rebirth, making this internal declaration: "I take absolute refuge in that very same Primeval Person from whom this ancient, cosmic manifestation has projected since the dawn of history!"

Thoroughly liberated from vanity and delusion, having conquered the crippling taint of attachment, permanently anchored in the knowledge of the inner Self (adhyatma-nityah), with all material cravings entirely dissolved, free from the dualities known as pleasure and pain— these clear-headed sages ascend straight to that imperishable, absolute State.

Neither the solar sun, nor the glowing moon, nor a blazing furnace can illuminate that supreme Abode. Having once ascended into that reality, a traveler never slides back into delusion; that represents My ultimate, absolute State.
simple_explanation: This verse clarifies that the highest spiritual realm is not a material location packed with physical stars or physical lights. It is the field of pure, self-luminous Consciousness. Physical light allows your eyes to see objects; Consciousness is that light which allows your mind to realize truth.

translation: An eternal fraction of My very own cosmic being (mamaivansho) manifests inside this living world as the individual conscious soul (Jiva). It anchors down and drags along the five physical senses and the processing mind, which belong to the domain of material nature.

When this conscious master of the biological framework leaves a physical body or transitions into a fresh one, it bundles up these sensory impressions and memory structures and moves along with them, exactly like the sweeping wind collects and carries fragrances away from their source sheets.
Governing and operating through the ear, the eye, the skin, the tongue, the nose, and the processing mind, this conscious entity tracks and experiences the sensory objects of the world.

The heavily deluded are entirely blind to its presence when it exits the physical shell, when it stays embedded inside matter, or when it experiences life through the modes of nature. But those who look through the sharp eye of wisdom (jnana-chakshushah) perceive it clearly.

Striving practitioners of Yoga directly perceive this conscious presence seated within their own selfhood. But those who are undisciplined and lack inner refinement (akritatmanah), can never see it, no matter how much dry, academic effort they make.

That brilliant radiance which resides within the solar sun and illuminates this entire universe, that which glows inside the moon, and that which burns inside a fire—know that energy to be an expression of My cosmic power (tat tejo viddhi mamakam).

Permeating the planet earth (gam-avishya), I stabilize and sustain all living structures by My raw, gravity-like energy. Becoming the moisture-laden cosmic moon (Soma), I nourish and pump life-juices into all the vegetation and crops.

I manifest as the metabolic fire of digestion (Vaishvanarah) operating inside the bodies of all living creatures. Coordinated with the inward (Prana) and outward (Apana) respiratory breaths, I digest the four distinct classes of food consumed.

I am permanently seated within the heart core of everyone. From My underlying presence radiates retentive memory, clear wisdom, and the dissolution of doubts (apohanam). I am the sole objective to be known across all the Vedas; I am the author of the ultimate conclusion of scripture (Vedanta-krit), and I am the genuine knower of the Veda.

There are two categories of entities functioning in this world—the Perishable (Kshara) and the Imperishable (Akshara). The physical bodies and changing forms of all living creatures constitute the Perishable; while the unmoving, silent Field of individual souls is designated as the Imperishable.

But entirely distinct from these two, there exists the absolute Supreme Person (Uttamah Purushah), celebrated by the title of the higher Self (Paramatma). He is the immutable, sovereign Lord who completely permeates all the three worlds and actively sustains their existence.

Because I transcend the Perishable universe and stand supreme above even the Imperishable soul-field, for this reason am I celebrated throughout worldly literature and across the sacred pages of the Vedas by the title of the Supreme Divine Person (Purushottamah).

He who, entirely free from the taint of delusion, understands Me in essence as this Supreme Divine Person—he becomes an all-knowing knower of reality (sarva-vit), O descendant of Bharata, and worships Me with his entire being.

Thus has this most profound, secret science been clearly unfolded by Me, O sinless one! Absorbing and practicing this truth, a human being unlocks his highest intelligence and completes all his historical obligations, O Bharata!
